- scripts/validate_process.sh:2192-2194 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The header comment of the `# BEGIN validation owner routing` block still says an invalid `VALIDATION_HARNESS_HEAL_ENABLED` value turns owner routing off, but `validation_owner_enabled()` now warns and returns 0, so routing stays on.
  WHY: An operator reading the only description of the kill-switch contract would expect routing to be off when it stays on. All reviewers rated this NIT. Gemini cited the range as lines 2179-2184.
- scripts/validate_process.sh:2211-2226 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The `VALIDATION_OWNER_SWITCH_WARNED` "warn once" guard is lost when `validation_owner_enabled` first runs inside a `$(...)` command substitution, such as `validation_owner_comment_marker` at line 2745. The `invalid_switch` warning is then printed again by the next direct call, such as `write_result_files` at line 2784.
  WHY: A subshell assignment does not propagate to the parent shell, so the warning is duplicated within one run. Other reviewers raised the same mechanism only as a hardening suggestion, not as a finding.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

  PROBLEM: The comment still says an invalid `VALIDATION_HARNESS_HEAL_ENABLED` value turns owner routing off, but the code now warns and keeps routing on.

- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: scripts/validate_process.sh `validation_owner_enabled` / `VALIDATION_OWNER_SWITCH_WARNED` (~2221-2224). The warned flag is lost in `$(...)` subshells, so the warning repeats. Suggested fix: use a sentinel file under `RUNTIME_DIR`. About 3-4 lines. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/validate_process.sh:2179-2184 (# BEGIN validation owner routing header comment) | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The header comment says an invalid `VALIDATION_HARNESS_HEAL_ENABLED` value turns owner routing off.
  WHY: The code now warns and stays enabled (return 0), so the comment may mislead operators.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: scripts/validate_process.sh `validation_owner_enabled()` / `VALIDATION_OWNER_SWITCH_WARNED` (2221-2224). The warning guard is lost in subshells, which can spam the log. Suggested fix: resolve the switch once into `_VALIDATION_OWNER_ENABLED`. About 8 lines. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/validate_process.sh:2211-2226, 2495-2498, 2745, 2784 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The "warn once" guard is lost when the first `validation_owner_enabled` call happens inside a command substitution, because a subshell assignment to `VALIDATION_OWNER_SWITCH_WARNED` does not propagate to the parent shell.
  WHY: In `fail_validate_codex_phase` the line 2745 substitution warns in a subshell, then `write_result_files` at line 2784 (via `validation_owner_merge_fields`) prints the same `invalid_switch` warning again.
- scripts/validate_process.sh:2192-2194 vs 2211-2226 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The header comment still says anything else is off with a warning, but the code now warns and leaves routing ON, matching the poller at `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2467-2474`.
  WHY: A declared-vs-effective gap on the kill switch. An operator setting `VALIDATION_HARNESS_HEAL_ENABLED=1` or `0` would expect routing off but get it on.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS:
  - scripts/validate_process.sh `validation_owner_load_bounced`, lines 2301-2308. Under `set -euo pipefail`, a jq failure empties the bounce-fingerprint file, but the `validation_harness_bounced_loaded` sentinel is still written unconditionally. The failed parse is memoised and never retried. Suggested fix: skip the sentinel and clear the file when the parse fails. About 4 lines.
  - scripts/validate_process.sh `validation_owner_enabled` (2211-2226) / `validation_owner_comment_marker` (2495-2498). The switch is re-parsed on every call and the warned state does not survive a command substitution. Suggested fix: compute `VALIDATION_OWNER_ENABLED` once at block load. About 8 lines.
  - HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

  WHY: An operator setting `VALIDATION_HARNESS_HEAL_ENABLED=1` expecting off behavior still gets failure classification and owner-routing fields.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: NONE. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 0

  PROBLEM: The header comment says "anything else is off with a warning", but `validation_owner_enabled()` (2211-2226) now warns once and returns 0, leaving routing on.
  WHY: There is no runtime failure, since the code matches the poller (`scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2467-2474`) and the new test. An operator reading the comment would still conclude `VALIDATION_HARNESS_HEAL_ENABLED=1` disables routing.

Suggested fix: a file-based sentinel via `validation_owner_runtime_file validation_owner_switch_warned`. About 3 lines. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
